card.name: Linking words in old scholarly prose
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as of, by, been, shall and manner inside long, formal sentences in 18th and 19th century scholarly or legal writing. Often right before a named author, a cited authority, or a repeated reference.

modes.label: Of/by before an author
modes.description: The word 'of' or 'by' introduces a named scientist's work, as in 'those of Hertwig'.
modes.example: Flourens' experiments have been confirmed by those<< of>> Hertwig in every particular, and

modes.label: Auxiliary or verb in formal clause
modes.description: Words like been, shall, already or I appear mid-clause in archaic argument or reporting.
modes.example: a similar parallelism in the forms of life has<< been>> observed by several authors; so it is

card.writes: The promoted tokens are 'mm' forms, which look unrelated to these contexts, so the output effect is unclear.
